title: Volume 4 · Warehouses, Transfers and Stock Counts
subtitle: Lessons 1–4: a warehouse tree that matches how the business moves goods, transfers that keep stock whole, and counts that post the truth
outcomes: Lay out a warehouse tree that operations and finance both accept
Transfer stock between warehouses without changing total quantity or value
Run a stock count and post the difference to the right account
Configure reorder rules so shortages surface before a customer does

slides.title: Design the warehouse tree before the first transfer
bullets: A warehouse is a location with a ledger, not a shelf, so each one must earn its place
Every warehouse has default accounts, and a wrong default quietly corrupts valuation
Goods In Transit only earns its place when goods genuinely leave one site and arrive at another
Create the tree before any transaction, because moving stock later leaves a migration trail

rows: Main - SM, parent All Warehouses, company SM
Retail Counter - SM, parent All Warehouses
Assembly Floor - SM, parent All Warehouses
Returns Quarantine - SM, parent All Warehouses
Stock account Stock In Hand - SM
Four leaves under one root, no orphans

slides.notes: Clients often want a warehouse per van, per salesperson or per shelf, which turns every report into noise. The test is simple: if you would never ask for the stock ledger of that location alone, it is not a warehouse. Four leaves cover most Malaysian distributors, and adding a fifth later is easy, whereas collapsing seven into four is a weekend of transfers.

slides.title: What each warehouse is actually for
bullets: Location names should describe physical truth, not reporting ambition
Quarantine keeps damaged or returned goods visible without counting them as sellable
Assembly floor stock is committed to production, so it belongs in a separate ledger
A retail counter needs its own ledger because its stock is priced and counted differently
slides.notes: This table is worth pasting into the configuration worksheet, because it converts a vague conversation into four decisions the client signs off. The quarantine warehouse is the one clients resist and later thank you for, since it stops returned goods being sold twice. If a client insists on one warehouse for everything, write down who will reconcile the differences each month.

slides.title: Move stock without changing who owns it
bullets: A material transfer shifts quantity between warehouses and leaves the total untouched
FIFO valuation travels with the goods, so the destination inherits the oldest layer
Transfer the quantity that physically moved, not the quantity you wish had moved
Use the Stock Entry transfer type, never a purchase and sale pair inside one company

rows: Source and target warehouse fields appear
From Main - SM, to Retail Counter - SM
Two rows: -5 at Main, +5 at Retail, same rate

slides.notes: Two ledger rows, one quantity, one valuation: that is what a transfer should look like. If the source and destination rates differ without a landed cost, someone has allowed different valuation on the destination warehouse, and the difference lands in a stock adjustment account that nobody owns. Check both rows every time until the client's team does it by habit.

slides.title: Two rows, one quantity, one valuation
bullets: A transfer should appear as one outgoing and one incoming row at the same rate
Total quantity and total value across the company must be identical before and after
A rate difference between the two rows means the destination warehouse has its own valuation
Stock in transit is only used when goods genuinely travel between sites

rows: Stock Ledger, filter the stock entry

slides.notes: Two rows at the same rate is what a clean transfer looks like, and anything else is a configuration problem rather than a stock problem. If the destination rate differs, the warehouse carries its own valuation method or its own stock account, and the difference will land in an adjustment account nobody owns. Check both rows before you move on to counting.

slides.title: Count the shelf and post the difference
bullets: Stock reconciliation is the only honest way to correct a quantity after a physical count
The difference posts to a stock adjustment account, which finance must recognise as a cost
Count before you post, and post once, because every reconciliation is a permanent ledger row
Reconciled units keep the current valuation rather than inventing a new one
slides.notes: Three units short is 360.00 of cost, and the client must decide whether that is shrinkage, a picking error or a missed delivery. The system will not make that call for them, and a consultant should not either. What you do insist on is a count sheet with a signature and a reason code, so the loss has an owner rather than appearing as an unexplained line in the profit and loss statement.

slides.title: Set reorder levels so shortages arrive early
bullets: Reorder level is the trigger, reorder quantity is the batch, and both belong in the item
The reorder report turns levels into a material request, which is the consultant-friendly path
Calculate lead time first: two units a day for seven days plus ten safety is twenty four
A reorder level set by feel produces either stockouts or dead stock within a quarter

rows: Main - SM, reorder level 24, reorder quantity 20
Tick the item as reorder enabled
Sell down to 22 units at Main

slides.notes: Twenty four is not a round number and that is the point: two units a day for seven days of lead time equals fourteen, plus ten of safety stock. When a client asks why not twenty, the arithmetic answers for you and they stop treating the number as taste. Pair the level with a reorder quantity that matches the supplier's carton, or every purchase order will carry an awkward remainder.

slides.kicker: Lesson 6 · Verify the count and the rule
slides.title: What the reports should say afterwards
bullets: Bin quantity, stock ledger total and stock balance must all agree after any movement
Total stock value across warehouses must be unchanged by transfers and cut only by counts
The reorder report is a to-do list, so it must be short and actionable
Any stock adjustment account balance is a conversation, not a rounding difference
slides.notes: Ask the learner to prove total value before and after: fifty units at one hundred twenty is six thousand, transfers change nothing, and a three unit shortage leaves forty seven units worth five thousand six hundred forty. When those three numbers agree, the warehouse model is sound and the client can be shown the reports without a caveat.

slides.title: Stock entry types and when to use them
bullets: Each stock entry type answers a different question, and choosing wrong leaves a ledger scar
Receipts and issues belong to purchases and production, not to ad-hoc corrections
Manufacture is the only type that consumes components and produces a finished item together
Repack converts one item into another, which suits bundling but not repricing
slides.notes: Consultants are asked to fix stock with a stock entry roughly once a week, and the honest answer is usually no. Show the client this table and ask which row their situation belongs to. If the answer is none, the real fix is in the process or the master data, and a stock entry would only hide the problem in a ledger account that nobody reads.

lab.title: Lab · Build the warehouse tree, transfer, count and reorder
steps: Create the four leaf warehouses under All Warehouses and set the stock account on each
Record the opening 50 units of SM-BL200 at Main at 120.00
Transfer 5 units from Main to Retail Counter and prove the total is unchanged
Read both stock ledger rows and confirm the rate carried across
Post a stock reconciliation to 47 units at Main with the stock adjustment account
Confirm the 360.00 posting and the new total value of 5,640.00
Set reorder level 24 and reorder quantity 20 on the item for Main warehouse
Sell down below 24 and confirm the item appears in the reorder report
lab.done: Done when both bins agree with the stock ledger, total value is 5,640.00, the stock adjustment account shows 360.00, and the reorder report lists only SM-BL200.

quiz.question: What does a material transfer do to total stock value?
options: Increases it by the transfer rate
quiz.why: A transfer moves quantity and value between warehouses within the same company, so the total quantity and total value are unchanged.

quiz.question: Which document corrects a quantity after a physical count?
options: Stock Entry of type Material Issue
quiz.why: Stock Reconciliation compares the counted quantity with the system quantity and posts the difference to a stock adjustment account.

quiz.question: With a reorder point of 2 units a day, 7 days of lead time and 10 units of safety stock, the level is what?
quiz.why: Demand during lead time is 2 × 7 = 14, plus 10 safety gives 24. Round numbers chosen by feel are how stockouts start.

quiz.question: Where does a stock reconciliation difference post?
options: The stock adjustment account you set
quiz.why: The difference posts to the stock adjustment account named on the document, which finance treats as an operating cost and reviews monthly.

quiz.question: Why keep a Returns Quarantine warehouse?
options: To avoid paying tax on returns
To keep returned goods visible but unsellable
quiz.why: Returned goods remain owned and valued, and quarantine makes that visible so nobody sells them again before inspection.

narration: Stock is the part of ERPNext where a small configuration mistake becomes a very large number. Start with the warehouse tree: four leaves, one root, each with the same stock account, because a wrong default account turns every transfer into a valuation difference. A material transfer moves five blenders from main to retail and leaves the total untouched, which is the check to make every single time. Then the stock count. Fifty units on the system, forty seven on the shelf, three units short at one hundred twenty is three hundred sixty of cost, and the reconciliation posts it to a stock adjustment account that finance must recognise. Finally the reorder rule: two units a day for seven days plus ten safety is twenty four, not a round twenty. Set those three things properly and the stock reports stop being arguments, and start being the evidence the client takes to their auditor at the first stock review.
